description: Route the reduced-block and cluster leaf eigendecompositions to cuSOLVER's BATCHED small-matrix eigensolvers (syevjBatched batched-Jacobi and/or syevdBatched batched-D&C) instead of the custom single-CTA SIMT megakernels mega_eigh_med_split_k (42% of shape 11, 66.7% barrier-latency-bound) and mega_eigh_clust_split_k (44.6% of shape 6, cross-CTA barrier-bound). Library substitution targeting the barrier-latency / launch-overhead bottleneck: one fused batched library call amortizes the many small leaf solves that the custom megakernels serialize on __syncthreads/cl.sync. Keep the per-matrix residual gate + cuSOLVER fallback; route guarded per shape.

t1: route sign-DC (shape 11) K=300 leaf stack (1280x300x300) to cusolverDnXsyevBatched (one batched syevd launch, eigenvectors returned directly, NO WY back-transform), via a private cuSOLVER handle + double cudaDeviceSynchronize ordering (no 'stream' token, leaderboard-clean). Residual gate + cuSOLVER fallback kept. 39/39 validate. shape 11: ~100ms(parent)->171.6ms; isolated leaf 119ms(cuSOLVER) vs 43.5ms(megakernel), ~2.7x. nsys: mega_eigh_med_split_k GONE, replaced by syevd internals (782 gemvx + symv + larfg + steqr). REGRESSION.

t2: route mixed-peel REST (shape 6) leaf stack (~250x512x512) to cusolverDnXsyevBatched; eigenvectors+ascending eigenvalues direct, so NO Newton-Schulz orthonormalization + NO Rayleigh re-eval (the cluster path's post-steps). Residual gate kept. 39/39 validate. shape 6: 107.3ms(parent)->126.0ms; isolated leaf 80.6ms(cuSOLVER) vs 51.2ms(cluster kernel), ~1.6x. nsys: mega_eigh_clust_split_k GONE (was 44.6%/45.2ms in parent), replaced by 780 gemvx + 256 symv + steqr. LEAST-BAD single route but still a regression.

t3: route ALL low-rank inner-solve leaves (shapes 2/3/8/12 dense/psd/rankdef k=256..384, mixed-peel dense/psd peel, sign-DC-large block eigh) to cusolverDnXsyevBatched. Residual gate kept. 39/39 validate. LARGEST regression: shape 3 78->119ms(+41), shape 8 85->140ms(+55), shape 5 90->115ms(+25), shape 4 46->73ms, shape 12 31->46ms. cuSOLVER's generic batched syevd is far slower than the megakernel + TF32 WY back-transform on k<=384 low-rank leaves.

t4: FULL substitution -- ALL leaf classes (sign-DC K=300 + mixed-peel rest n=512 + low-rank inner k<=384) routed to cusolverDnXsyevBatched, guarded per shape. 39/39 validate. geomean 35850us (+25.6%), the aggregate of t1+t2+t3: shape 6 155.4ms (both rest+LR peel batched), shape 11 171.9ms, shape 8 140ms. The brief's mechanism (one fused batched library call replaces the barrier-bound megakernels) works and validates, but cuSOLVER's generic n>32 batched syevd re-incurs MORE launch/latency overhead than the fused megakernels amortize.

t5 (FINAL state): rest-only batched route (least-bad single substitution; sign-DC + low-rank kept on megakernels). geomean 28960us (+1.5% vs parent 28537). shape 6 126.0ms, shape 11 99.9ms (untouched floor). 39/39 validate. ncu on shape-6 cuSOLVER cuds_symv_lo_direct_kernel: 51.2% cycles stalled on scoreboard/L1TEX dependency, 0.72 issued-warps/scheduler, 256 symv+780 gemvx launches -- the latency-bound SIMT syevd machinery the megakernel fuses away, batch-looped. syevjBatched (batched Jacobi, the brief's primary API) is documented n<=32 only, cannot take the K=300/n=512 leaves; XsyevBatched is the only n>32 batched API and loses on every leaf class.

Built + measured the batched-cuSOLVER leaf substitution end-to-end on the live path across all 5 trials; parent 28537us. A leaderboard-clean batched-eigensolver bridge now exists in submission.py (compiles with -lcusolver, 0 'stream' tokens, 39/39 validate): C++ syev_batched wraps cusolverDnXsyevBatched with a private cached handle ordered by double cudaDeviceSynchronize (torch's at::cuda::getCurrentCUDASolverDnHandle is NOT exported in this build, so I created my own handle; stream-binding is banned by the harness). Python _syev_batched_cusolver returns torch-convention (lam ascending, Q) with the column-major->row-major transpose fixed (residual 8e-6, verified). Three opt-in per-shape route knobs: _SIGN_DC_BATCHED_LEAF, _REST_BATCHED_LEAF, _LR_BATCHED_LEAF.

MEASURED (all regress vs parent): t1 sign-DC K=300 leaves->batched: 29778us (+4.3%, shape11 ~100->171.6ms). t2 rest n=512 leaves->batched: 28983us (+1.6%, shape6 107.3->126.0ms) -- LEAST-BAD. t3 low-rank k<=384 leaves->batched: 34054us (+19.3%, shape3 +41ms, shape8 +55ms). t4 all-on: 35850us (+25.6%). t5 final=rest-only: 28960us. FINAL committed state 6564cd68b = rest-only (closest to parity).

WHY IT LOSES (nsys+ncu confirmed): the substitution DID replace the barrier-bound megakernels -- mega_eigh_clust_split_k GONE from shape6, mega_eigh_med_split_k GONE from shape11. But cusolverDnSsyevjBatched (the brief's PRIMARY batched-Jacobi API) is documented n<=32 ONLY (N<=16 has an OOB bug) -- our leaves are K=300/n=512, so it cannot take them. cusolverDnXsyevBatched is the ONLY n>32 batched API, and for n>32 it dispatches the SAME serial syevd machinery batch-looped: nsys shows 780 gemvx + 256 cuds_symv_lo_direct + larfg + steqr launches per shape; ncu on the symv shows 51.2% cycles stalled on scoreboard/L1TEX dependency, 0.72 issued-warps/scheduler -- the exact latency-bound SIMT pattern the custom single-CTA/cross-CTA megakernels FUSE AWAY (one resident CTA, SMEM stage hand-off, no per-launch latency). Isolated leaf timings: sign-DC 119ms(cuSOLVER) vs 43.5ms(mega); rest 80.6ms vs 51.2ms(cluster); torch.linalg.eigh looped 115ms/83.7ms. The megakernels beat cuSOLVER's batched path on EVERY leaf class because they were purpose-built to amortize exactly this overhead.

OPEN DIRECTIONS I did not reach: (1) cuSOLVERDx (device-side, header-only, kernel-embeddable eigensolver) supports batched symmetric eig with NO n<=32 cap -- a genuinely-parallel batched dense solver could beat both if it fuses the panel loop; needs a from-scratch device kernel (big). (2) syevjBatched IS fast for n<=32 -- if a leaf class could be pre-reduced to <=32 sub-blocks (e.g. a batched tridiag reduction then a <=32 tridiag Jacobi) the batched-Jacobi win the brief targets might materialize. (3) The rest path's -1.6% gap is small; the cluster kernel wins mostly via its NS-skip -- a cheaper rest solve (e.g. tighter cluster C sweep, or a batched-Jacobi finish on already-tridiagonalized blocks) is unexplored. (4) I did not try the non-batched syevj with tuned sweeps/tolerance (loops per matrix, likely also a loss but unmeasured). Recommend the manager not pursue further cuSOLVER-batched substitution on these leaf sizes (measured dead across the board) unless via cuSOLVERDx or a leaf-size reduction to n<=32.

t6 cuSOLVERDx availability probe (coordinator's #1 lever): one load_inline build attempt with #include <cusolverdx.hpp> -> 'fatal error: cusolverdx.hpp: No such file or directory'. cuSOLVERDx/MathDx is NOT present in this toolchain: no headers on the filesystem (only a tutorial PDF), not in the CUDA 13.3 toolkit include dir, no nvidia-mathdx pip wheel, no /opt|/usr/local MathDx root. TWO-fold dead: (1) unavailable here; (2) even if pip-installed locally it is NON-PORTABLE to the remote leaderboard build (layout.md: custom CUDA must build against STOCK headers only; extra_include_paths to a local checkout is diagnostic-only), so a cuSOLVERDx submission.py cannot be built/submitted remotely regardless. HEAD stays at the committed final trial 5 (6564cd68b, rest-only batched route, 28960us). No ncu comparison possible (no kernel to profile). This maps the vendor-device-library angle as unreachable in this environment -- the hand-written-Jacobi side a sibling attacks is the remaining route to a fused batched leaf primitive.

FULL brief-81 picture (parent 28537us, HEAD=6564cd68b final):
- Host cuSOLVER batched API (Xsyev n>32) measured DEAD as a leaf solver across all classes: t1 sign-DC 29778us(+4.3%), t2 rest 28983us(+1.6%, least-bad), t3 low-rank 34054us(+19.3%), t4 all-on 35850us(+25.6%). nsys: it replaced the barrier-bound megakernels but is a batch-LOOP over serial syevd (780 gemvx + 256 symv/shape); ncu on its symv: 51.2% scoreboard-stalled, 0.72 warps/sched. Isolated leaf: cuSOLVER 119ms(signDC)/80.6ms(rest) vs MEGAKERNEL 43.5ms/51.2ms -- the custom fused kernels already beat it.
- syevjBatched (batched Jacobi, the brief's primary API) is n<=32 only -> cannot take K=300/n=512 leaves.
- cuSOLVERDx (would have NO n<=32 cap) is unavailable + non-portable.
Net: BOTH vendor batched-eigensolver routes (host cuSOLVER, device cuSOLVERDx) are exhausted/unreachable on these K~300-512 leaf sizes. A fused batched leaf primitive that beats the megakernel must be HAND-WRITTEN (the sibling's hand-Jacobi angle) or reached via a leaf-size reduction to n<=32 so syevjBatched applies -- neither is on brief-81. The bridge I built (syev_batched C++ wrapper + _syev_batched_cusolver + 3 per-shape route knobs, leaderboard-clean, 39/39, committed) remains available if a future leaf class lands in a regime where cuSOLVER's batch-loop wins. Final committed state = rest-only route (28960us); manager won't pick it as a parent since it regresses, but it captures the closest-to-parity measured substitution rather than a revert.
